explanation: A mutex lock is a synchronization mechanism in C programming that ensures only one thread can access a shared resource at a time. It is used to prevent race conditions in multithreaded applications, maintaining data integrity and avoiding conflicts when multiple threads attempt to modify the same data simultaneously.
code_example: printf("Thread acquired the lock.\n");  // Critical section
example_explanation: This example demonstrates the mutex lock by initializing a mutex, creating a single thread that acquires the lock, prints a message in the critical section, and then unlocks it. The main thread waits for the created thread to finish, showing how pthread_mutex_lock ensures exclusive access to the shared resource, preventing concurrent modifications.
